record.paper_title: Observational Cosmology: caveats and open questions in the standard model
record.original_question: Does the temperature of the intergalactic medium, as inferred from the small-scale falloff of the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum, evolve with redshift as expected from adiabatic cooling in an expanding universe, or is the reported absence of redshift evolution evidence that requires another explanation?

evidence.quote: It is typically inferred to be 20000 K, but there is no evidence of evolution with redshift[80]. Yet in the Big Bang, that temperature ought to adiabatically decrease as space expands everywhere.

If these measurements are confirmed by other means, it could be another indicator that the universe is not really expanding unless other explanations arise. At present it is early to establish definitively this claim.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the diffuse intergalactic medium (IGM), the low-density baryonic gas pervading the universe between galaxies, whose thermal state can be probed observationally through the Lyman-alpha forest: the dense series of absorption lines blueward of the Lyman-alpha emission of distant quasars produced by neutral hydrogen along the line of sight. On small spatial scales, the one-dimensional flux power spectrum of the Lyman-alpha forest exhibits a high-wavenumber cutoff arising from thermal Doppler broadening and pressure (Jeans) smoothing, from which one can infer a characteristic IGM temperature T_0 at the cosmic mean density as a function of redshift z.

In a homogeneous, isotropically expanding universe with scale factor a(t), a non-relativistic ideal gas that is thermally decoupled and undergoes no additional heating or cooling cools adiabatically as T ∝ a^{-2} ∝ (1+z)^2, so T_0(z) should decrease monotonically toward lower redshift in the absence of compensating heat sources.

Question: Does the IGM temperature T_0(z), as inferred from the small-scale cutoff of the Lyman-alpha forest flux power spectrum across the observable redshift range (roughly 2 ≲ z ≲ 5), evolve with redshift in a manner consistent with adiabatic cooling in an expanding Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker universe (possibly modified by photoionization heating during and after hydrogen and helium reionization, Compton cooling off the cosmic microwave background, and structure-formation shock heating)? Equivalently, can the observed redshift dependence of T_0 inferred from the Lyman-alpha forest be reproduced by a standard thermal-history model in an expanding universe, or does it require some non-standard explanation?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent measurements of the Lyman-alpha forest 1D flux power spectrum (e.g., Walther et al. 2019 and subsequent work) have constrained IGM thermal evolution from z ≈ 5.4 down to z ≈ 1.8 and find a redshift evolution of T_0 broadly consistent with standard thermal-history models that include hydrogen and helium reionization heating followed by cooling. Tensions remain at the highest redshifts (z ≳ 5) where inferred temperatures are lower than expected. The early claim of "no redshift evolution" has not been supported by later, more precise measurements; the question is largely resolved in favor of standard expanding-universe thermal histories, though detailed thermal modeling is ongoing.

status_evidence.title: New Constraints on IGM Thermal Evolution from the Lyα Forest Power Spectrum
status_evidence.snippet: Measurements of IGM thermal evolution over z = 5.4 to z = 1.8 using the Lyα forest power spectrum; results consistent with photoionization heating from reionization followed by cooling.
status_evidence.claim: Observed redshift evolution of T_0 from the Lyman-alpha forest power spectrum is consistent with standard thermal-history models in an expanding universe.

status_evidence.title: Cutoff in the Lyman-α forest power spectrum: Warm IGM or warm dark matter?
status_evidence.snippet: The small-scale cutoff of the Lyα forest power spectrum constrains IGM temperature and pressure smoothing as functions of redshift.
status_evidence.claim: The small-scale cutoff is sensitive to redshift evolution of IGM temperature.

status_evidence.title: Lognormal Simulations of the Lyman α Forest: Thermal History of the IGM
status_evidence.snippet: Recent thermal-history reconstructions show T_0 evolves with redshift in line with standard reionization-driven heating and subsequent cooling.
status_evidence.claim: Updated analyses find clear redshift evolution of T_0 in agreement with standard cosmology.
